acceptance_checks.acceptance: No command execution or sensitive response echo occurs and request size is bounded.
acceptance_checks.evidence: TestDecoyRecordsMetadataOnlyInteraction drives the real handler against the real C05 store: one accepted request commits exactly one version 1 http.request observation whose metadata holds only the path. TestDecoyNeverEchoesRequestContent sends the synthetic marker in the query, the header and the body: the fixed answer and the committed bytes contain the marker nowhere. TestDecoyBoundsRequestSize rejects a declared and an observed body above the bound with 413 and commits nothing, and accepts a body exactly at the bound. TestDecoyNeverExecutesCommandsOrEgresses parses every file of the decoy package, requires its exact import set, resolves the local name of the net/http import from its declaration, rejects a dot import and checks every identifier the package takes from net/http, so only the handler API is allowed: the package cannot open a file, run a process or dial a remote service, and an outbound client call fails the anchor under any import name. strace -f -e trace=network,execve over the focused test binary recorded zero network syscalls and exactly one execve, the test binary itself.

negative_case_checks.case: Missing prerequisites, malformed fixtures or unavailable required providers produce an explicit error rather than placeholder success.
negative_case_checks.evidence: TestDecoyFailsClosedOnMissingPrerequisites covers the six construction cases of the fixture: a missing store, a missing clock, an invalid identity, a zero request bound, a zero path bound and a request bound above the version 1 event limit all return decoy.ErrInvalidInput. A closed store answers 503 with the fixed unavailable body instead of the accepted body. The six rejected requests of the fixture answer 405, 413 and 400 with their fixed bodies and commit nothing. No provider is required by this slice; a missing provider cannot silently succeed because none is used.

negative_case_checks.case: Repeat after restart and verify the declared invariant and documented recovery outcome.
negative_case_checks.evidence: TestDecoyObservationsSurviveRestart accepts a sensor-01 event, records a decoy observation, closes and reopens the store, rebuilds the decoy and records another observation: the store holds the sensor event plus the two decoy observations with the contiguous decoy-01 sequence 1 and 2. The rebuild recovers the sequence from the durable history, so there is no duplicate and no gap. A decoy whose identity has a non-contiguous history fails closed with storage.ErrRecovery instead of renumbering.

The decoy package has no listener, no client and no outbound call: the import allowlist of TestDecoyNeverExecutesCommandsOrEgresses admits only the standard HTTP, hashing, JSON and text packages and the existing contract, sensor and storage packages, and its net/http identifier allowlist admits only the handler API under the local name resolved from the import declaration, so a client call such as http.DefaultClient.Do, an aliased web.DefaultClient.Do, a dot import and a second package file are all rejected by the anchor. The focused test binary recorded zero network syscalls under strace. Container isolation and egress denial for a published decoy remain the C13 work and are not claimed here.

security_review.verification: The decoy reuses the C04 version 1 event contract and the C05 publication path through sensor.Accept; the observation is validated by the existing contract before it is committed.
security_review.atomicity: One observation is committed under the existing single-writer lock. The sequence advances only after the store accepted the record, so a rejected or failed observation leaves no gap in the accepted history.
security_review.data_bounds: The request body is bounded by the explicit deployment bound and read only to enforce it. The recorded path is bounded in bytes, must be valid UTF-8 and must not contain control characters. The assembled observation stays inside the version 1 event payload limit.
security_review.echo: Every answer is a fixed constant: no request-derived value, no internal state and no error detail reaches the caller. The query, the headers and the body are discarded and never recorded. The recorded path is never resolved against a file, a command or a URL. The package takes no client identifier from net/http: the anchor resolves the local import name, rejects a dot import, scans every file of the package and admits only the handler API.
security_review.filesystem: The decoy opens no file. The durable bytes are written by the existing C05 adapter with its 0700/0600 ownership, atomic manifest publication and directory flush.
security_review.known_limits: The local clock and the private store remain trusted. The recorded path can contain an attacker-chosen value by design, because the path is the observation; it is never executed or resolved. A second decoy instance on the same store can lose a sequence race and then answers 503 instead of committing a conflicting observation.
